egress.terms: 2.5 TB a month on a 10 Gbps port for this rung, stated in the plan row as 'bw: 2.5 TB @ 10Gbps'; no overage price is published

tooling: order links go to my.hostbrr.com/order/config/index/largeram with a group and pricing id; DDoS mitigation is described as always-on with instant mitigation; no API appears on the page read
chaining: EUR 2.00 for 2 GB and 25 GB of NVMe on a 10 Gbps port in Frankfurt is the cheapest plan per gigabyte of RAM outside InterServer, and 2.5 TB at 10 Gbps suits a mirror or a package cache in the EU; the USD 1.44 IPv6-only row is cheaper still but at 1 Gbps and without IPv4, which rules out anything that has to reach an IPv4-only client

limits.value: 2.5 TB a month of transfer on a 10 Gbps port
2.5 TB against a 10 Gbps port is a two-hour burst at line rate, so the transfer cap binds long before the port does

limits_note: 2.5 TB a month on Value 2GB at a 10 Gbps port. The tracker's cheapest USD 1.44 row carries the same 2,500 GB but on a 1 Gbps port and IPv6 only, so the cheaper row is the same allowance at a tenth of the throughput and without an IPv4 address. No overage price and no post-allowance throttle are stated on the page read.
binding_note: 2.5 TB a month on a 10 Gbps port is the mismatch: the port can move the whole allowance in about 33 minutes, so the monthly transfer is what actually limits use.

notes: This fills the 4 GiB rung that the earlier read could not render: the selector is a JavaScript category filter and every plan lives in a `plans = [...]` array in the page source, so a fetch plus a parse of that array returns all ten rows. The 4 GiB rung is USD 3.25 a month monthly, or USD 32.50 a year (USD 2.71 a month) on annual prepay. It sits under the USD 5 line but well below the 8 GiB winner, and its 2.5 TB allowance on a 10 Gbps port is the thinnest part of the offer. The 8 GiB rung is USD 5.50 and therefore over the line. Not established: the payment rails and any card hold; whether the monthly price carries a first-term discount (no strike-through or renewal note is present in the array).

extras.price_arithmetic: USD 3.25 a month billed monthly as published by the vendor, no conversion applied; annual prepay is USD 32.50, which is USD 2.708 a month and USD 32.50 out of pocket. A VPS bills whether it runs or not, so the 24/7 and 10 h/day figures are the same number.
extras.renewal_note: the array carries both the monthly and the yearly rate and no first-term price, so the renewal is the published monthly figure
extras.ipv6: not stated for this rung in the array; the corpus records IPv6 on the IPv6-only product line

benchmark.note: Ryzen 9 3900 at 3.09 GHz. One of the few rows where the price and the measured package are the same line of text.

extras.refund: 7 days on a VPS paid by card or PayPal, 30 days on shared; crypto none

confidence_note: the whole plan ladder, including this rung, is held in a JavaScript array on the vendor's page and is not rendered into the DOM until a category tab is clicked, which is why the earlier read showed only the default plan. Prices are published in both EUR and USD by the vendor; the USD figures are recorded and no conversion was applied.
